title: Independent audit of PLAY-02 synthetic viewer projection privacy and Director-requested integration into main
actor: Claude Code agent (architect/QA reviewer role) on Director request, local WSL session

changes.description: Audited Codex commit 780c26e (PLAY-02, CHG-20261014-004) against ADR0014, the viewer contract, blueprint §§6.2/6.4/7.5/13 and the backlog acceptance (opponent hand/deck identity absent from every transport/resource/log/export path). The review covered: the closed TypeBox DTO and surface/diagnostic codecs (bounded bytes, no accessor evaluation, fixed outcomes); the projector's allowlist (fronts for play/discard/own hand/authorized reveals, backs elsewhere, normal-inking reveal correlated by state ID to the actual inked card, front-only metadata normalization, slot-derived back references, ref-sorted private zones, recipient-scoped reveal history without object links); the resolver's per-move field profile; the two-line kernel bridge `inspect` and its absence from Lab RPC; HMAC viewer-key domain separation from the RNG stream, with zeroing on dispose; the projection-only worker reply; and the participant-only read-only committed `view` with pin and post-condition checks. Verdict: PLAY-02 acceptance is met for the supported two-player synthetic scope; no blocking finding.

Independent runs RUN-20261014-064..069 all passed at Codex's final fingerprint e3a9578b with exact timing and 0 redactions. RUN064: full verify:foundation (307 project checks = 283 Node + 24 Python; 406 upstream passes/1 inherited skip; 2 injection). RUN065: auditor real-engine probe. Each instance was relabelled with a unique definition so hidden identity is meaningful. Paired hidden worlds differed by renamed/reshuffled hidden instances, hidden definitions, metadata/controller and raw G/ctx/event noise; they gave 495 byte-identical encodings across three viewers at every revision of a complete game, with 369 positive controls. A second complete game was driven only through references: 55 read-only/restored revisions; 4,834 stale, 1,746 cross-viewer, 1,480 public and 432 raw references rejected. RUN066: auditor live PostgreSQL view probe. Adapter equality held at 13 committed versions under 16-way concurrency; 24 views racing a commit each saw the old or new state; 16 INVALID_REQUEST without accessors; FORBIDDEN for outsider/missing; PIN_UNAVAILABLE; six checkpoint forgeries failed closed; a 48-view burst served 34 and refused 14; restart reproduced; terminal hands stayed private. RUN067: boundary/bundle/migration probe (340 browser and 60 server imports refused; Lab never calls inspect; no server markers in bundles; vendor diff is the bridge only, kernel 896,076 bytes; migrations and privileges unchanged). RUN068: Codex database suites (5 + 3 + 11, eight identities). RUN069: Chromium 7 scenarios + 2 Lab workers. RUN070: docs:check covers this record.

Publication review of the two unpublished clock-documentation commits carried by the branch (e36d223, 3983e1c; CHG-20261014-001..003): documentation and evidence only, with no source change. Decoded Windows/WSL archives contain no hostname, hardware/account identifier, email or credential. The only identifiers are two public time.windows.com NTP addresses and the Windows account path segment already present in the published handoff. No private .env.local/database credential value appears in the branch diff; the three token-pattern matches are the scanner's own regular expression.

Follow-ups recorded, none blocking: (1) PLAY-03 must route every client command through the current-reference resolver; the internal service submit still accepts raw engine identities, which is safe only while no client ingress exists. (2) References include the opponent's anonymous ink backs and resolve server-side; today the engine rejects uniformly (DEFENDER_NOT_IN_PLAY) and the service stores only invalid_intent, but real-card outcomes must stay independent of hidden identity, or resolvable references must be restricted per field. (3) Each view restores by full re-execution in a fresh worker, sharing the 2-active/32-queued capacity: about 205-256 ms per concurrent pair for a 16-version game. PLAY-03 needs per-version caching and request limits (extends the PLAY-01 restore-cost follow-up). (4) The projector fails closed above 4,096 raw engine events; synthetic play uses about 7.2 per accepted move, so real-card matches must be measured. (5) The participant move list and the conservative under-card/inkwell visibility defaults must be rechecked during real-card certification. (6) Naming only: the Lab and upstream.lock.json still say pending_PLAY-02; the Lab's hidden-state refusal is correct.

Appended a dated independent-audit section to docs/validation/play-02.md and dated audit notes to ADR0014, the PLAY-02 plan and the viewer-privacy runbook. Added the audit sentence to the PLAY-02 paragraph of AGENTS.md, README.md and docs/README.md. Rewrote HANDOFF for the audit state. Added the audit to the F-VIEWER-PRIVACY description and RUN064..069 evidence. Corrected the stale F-ENGINE 'PLAY-02 wire/log privacy pending' to point to F-VIEWER-PRIVACY. Updated the F-VIEWER-PRIVACY table cell and added the PLAY-02 backlog evidence link to this record (status unchanged).

Local isolated CI was not rerun. During the audit the container clock stepped about 91 ms every 30 s (about 1.1 s over the six-minute pipeline, consistent with Codex's clock-rejected RUN051), and the Director declined environment repair; the PLAY-01 host memory incident also argues for one heavy run at a time. Hosted Foundation qualification is dispatched on the published audit branch before main is fast-forwarded and observed again on main; both run IDs are recorded in a later change.
